div.head: Rect 4.3, 4.3a, 4.3b, 4.3c
div.ab: [4.3] On ðam sylfum lande, ðe ðeos ræden on stænt, gebure gebyreð, þæt him man to landsetene sylle II oxan ⁊ I cu ⁊ VI sceap ⁊ VII æceras gesawene on his gyrde landes. [4.3a] Forðige ofer þæt gear ealle gerihtu, ðe him to gebyrigean. [4.3b] ⁊ sylle him man tol to his weorce ⁊ andlaman to his huse. [4.3c] Ðonne him forðsi[ð] gebyrige, gyme his hlaford ðæs he læfe.

In ipsa terra, ubi hec consuetudo stat, moris est, ut ad terram assidendam dentur ei duo boues et una uacca et VI oues et VII acre seminate in sua uirgata terrę. [4.3a] Post illum annum faciat omnes rectitudines, que ad eum attinent. [4.3b] Et committantur ei tela ad opus suum et suppellex ad domum suam. [4.3c] Si mortem obeat, rehabeat dominus suus omnia.

On ðam sylfum lande ðe ðeos ræden on stænt gebu|re gebyreð þæt him man to landsetene sylle . ii. oxan. 7. i. cu . 7. vi.sceap.7 vii . æceras ge|sawene on his gyrde landes. forðige ofer þæt gear ealle gerihtu ðe him to gebyrigean . 7 sylle him man tol to his weorce 7 andlaman to his huse . ðonne him forðsit [read as 6 ‘sið’] gebyrige gy|me his hlaford ðæs he læfe.

On ðam sylfum lande ðe ðeos ræden on stænt, gebure gebyreð þæt him man to landsetene sylle II oxan and I cu and VI sceap and VII æceras gesawene on his gyrde landes. Forðige ofer þæt gear ealle gerihtu, ðe him to gebyrigean. And sylle him man tol to his weorce and andlaman to his huse. Ðonne him forðsið gebyrige, gyme his hlaford ðæs he læfe.

Auf demselben Gute, auf dem obige Regelung gilt, kommt dem Bauern zu, dass man ihm als Bodeninventar 2 Ochsen und 1 Kuh und 6 Schafe und auf seine ‘Ruthe’ Landes 7 Äcker besät übergebe. [4.3a] Er vollziehe nach diesem [Antritts]jahr alle Rechtspflichten, die ihm zukommen. [4.3b] Und man gebe ihm Werkzeug für seine Arbeit und Geräthe für sein Haus. [4.3c] Wenn ihn der Tod trifft, halte sich sein Herr an das, was er hinterlässt.

[4.3] On the same estate where the above arrangement holds, it is due to the gebur that [the lord] should give him as stock for the land [for settling the holding] 2 oxen and 1 cow and 6 sheep, and 7 acres sown on his yardland [usually ¼ hide, 30 acres]. [4.3a] After that [first] year let him perform all the duties that are due from him. [4.3b] And let [the lord] give him tools for his work and utensils for his house. [4.3c] When death befalls him, let his lord take charge of what he [the gebur] leaves [on account of the farm stock].

On the same estate which this custom stands, it is fitting to give to the peasant [as needed] for settling the land, two oxen and one cow and six sheep and seven acres [already] sewn on his strip of land. After the [first] year is over he must fulfil all the duties which pertain to him. And one should give to him tools for his work and utensils for his house. When he dies, the lord should care for that which he leaves [behind].

On the same estate on which this custom is observed, it is appropriate that the tenant farmer be given for the cultivation of the land two oxen, one cow, six sheep, and seven acres already sown on his allotment of land. Let him perform all the duties assigned to him over the course of the year. And let him be given the tools for his labor and the utensils for his house. When he dies, his lord should oversee whatever he leaves behind.

zur Landbesiedlung, indem sie die Bauernhofstelle besetzt
for settling the land, by occupying the peasant's holding

Wohl nicht ‘Besetzung (occupation; Toller) des Landes’ (Schmid). Der Zeitpunkt (so auch Leo, Kemble, Seebohm EHR 1892, 459) ist, weil selbstverständlich, schwerlich ausgedrückt, auch wäre æt als Präposition natürlicher. Seten ‘Handlung des Besiedelns’ ist nicht nachgewiesen, wohl aber ‘Pflanzung, bestelltes Land’. Vielleicht diese Bed. hat landseten in der Überschrift zur Grenzbeschreibung eines Landguts in Urk. a. 903 Birch 600. ‘Landbesitz’ versteht da Toller, vielleicht eher ‘Gutsbestand’

Probably not ‘occupation of the land’ (Schmid; ‘occupation’ Toller). The point in time (so too Leo, Kemble, Seebohm EHR 1892, 459) is hardly expressed, since it goes without saying; and æt would also be more natural as the preposition. Seten ‘act of settling’ is not attested, but ‘plantation, cultivated land’ is. landseten perhaps has this meaning in the heading of the boundary description of an estate in charter a. 903 Birch 600. Toller understands ‘landed property’ there; perhaps rather ‘estate holding’
Zur Hufe gehörte normal ein Pfluggespann mit 8 Ochsen, daher zur Viertelhufe 2 Ochsen; Vinogradoff Growth 233. Diese sind denn auch das Heriot einer Virgate zu Worcester im 12. Jh.; ebd. 161
A hide normally had a plough-team of 8 oxen, and hence a quarter-hide 2 oxen; Vinogradoff Growth 233. These are indeed also the heriot of a virgate at Worcester in the 12th cent.; ibid. 161

Dreifelderwirtschaft (s. d. Gl) vermutet hieraus nach Seebohm Andrews Manor 163f.: der im September neu Einziehende bringe das laut 4, 2 vom Eingesessenen geforderte Saatkorn für 3 Äcker nicht mit. Daher erhalte er nur 7 Äcker (nicht 10, d. i. ¹/₃ seiner Gerte Landes, die Winterflur) besäet; Cunningham Growth § 34, Dt. Übs. S. 89⁶ zweifelt

Following Seebohm, Andrews Manor 163f. infers from this a three-field system (see that word in Gl): the man newly entering in September, he argues, does not bring with him the seed-corn for 3 acres demanded of the established tenant by 4, 2, and therefore receives only 7 acres sown (not 10, i.e. ¹/₃ of his yard of land, the winter field); Cunningham Growth § 34, German transl. p. 89⁶, has doubts
die Herrschaft
the lordship
Possessiv bedeutet oft (4, 2c. 6. 6, 2. 14 f.) Obliegenheit, Last
The possessive often (4, 2c. 6. 6, 2. 14 f.) denotes obligation, burden
wegen des Hofinventars; vgl. 5, 5
on account of the farm stock; cf. 5, 5
der Bauer
the peasant
Nicht ‘das Jahr hindurch’ (Leo, Schmid). Vor der ersten Ernte ist der Neusiedler zu jenen Leistungen unfähig
Not ‘throughout the year’ (Leo, Schmid). Before the first harvest the new settler is incapable of those services
Wie Haus und Vieh, so zählt auch das Gerät zum Gutsinventar. Der Bauer zieht völlig arm an; 4, 3c. Vgl. Gl Erbgang 9b
Like the house and livestock, the implements too count as estate stock. The peasant enters on his holding entirely without means; 4, 3c. Cf. Gl Erbgang 9b

Nicht ‘sorge für den Nachlass’ (Leo, Schmid). Die Wörter für Sorge, wie mhd. kummer, engl. distress, bedeuten auch ‘Arrest, Beschlagnahme’.—Nur durch Schenkung behielt der Hintersass das Gutsinventar als Eigen [ein Freilasser um 1050 verordnet, þat hi habben alle þinge, þe hi under honde habben, buten þat land; doch sind dies frühere Sklaven; Thorpe Dipl. 582]. Daneben kann er laut 5, 5 ‘freie’ Fahrhabe besitzen: Erwirtschaftetes oder Miteingebrachtes. Dagegen jenes Gutsinventar nimmt der Herr zurück: rehabeat Q. Vgl. Vinogradoff Villain. 176; Growth 286

Not ‘take care of the estate left behind’ (Leo, Schmid). The words for care, like M.H.G. kummer, Engl. distress, also mean ‘arrest, seizure’.—Only by gift did the tenant keep the estate stock as his own [a manumitter c. 1050 orders þat hi habben alle þinge, þe hi under honde habben, buten þat land; but these are former slaves; Thorpe Dipl. 582]. Besides this, according to 5, 5, he can possess ‘free’ chattels: what he has earned or brought in with him. That estate stock, on the other hand, the lord takes back: rehabeat Q. Cf. Vinogradoff Villain. 176; Growth 286
